question: Why is atenolol short, and what do we do?

steps.title: Our stock in three hospitals
steps.purpose: Read on-hand stock and 28-day use where each hospital keeps it.
steps.finding: 3 stock lines across 3 hospitals, 1 presentation, in units of use.

steps.title: Where our supply is made
steps.purpose: Follow each product's label to the plants it names, and place each plant in FDA's registration file.
steps.finding: 1 plant links on 1 labels; 1 placed in FDA's registration file.

steps.title: What FDA says about this shortage
steps.purpose: Read FDA's current shortage list and its history for this drug.
steps.finding: Not on FDA's current shortage list.

steps.title: Who else makes it
steps.purpose: List every labeler of this drug in the same form, and the plants their labels name.
steps.finding: 40 labelers make it in this form.

steps.title: What FDA found at those plants
steps.purpose: Read every FDA drug inspection, warning letter, import alert and recall for these plants.
steps.finding: 54 inspections (1 OAI at our plants), 4 compliance actions, 0 import-alert listings, 0 recalls.

steps.title: What FDA wrote at the OAI inspections
steps.purpose: Read the Form 483 observations recorded at those inspections.

steps.title: What our P&T committee already approved
steps.purpose: Read Corvale General's approved interchanges for these items.

steps.title: Which links can't be trusted
steps.purpose: Run the semantic layer's key rules (NDC and unit of use) over each hospital's stock, and name the rows they reject.
steps.finding: 11 stock rows across the system fail the NDC rule; 0 of them are this drug. Every row is in a shared unit of use.

steps.title: What we decided last time
steps.purpose: Recall past decisions on this drug from H-MEM, with who approved them.
steps.finding: No past decisions on this drug.

explanation.headline: Atenolol is not on FDA's shortage list; supply at Corvale East is 6.4 days and a transfer from Corvale Lakeside is the top option

sentences.text: FDA's drug shortage list does not include atenolol as of 2026-10-21.
Corvale East holds 105 tablets of atenolol 25 mg with a daily use of 16.5, giving 6.4 days on hand.
Corvale Lakeside holds 80 tablets of atenolol 25 mg with a daily use of 3.2, giving 25.1 days on hand.
The rule‑ranked option 1 is to transfer 35 tablets of 25 mg from Corvale Lakeside to Corvale East, which would leave Lakeside with 14 days and bring East to 8 days.
Bryant Ranch Prepack's plant (FEI 1000519407) was last inspected on 2026-07-16 and classified VAI.

rejected.text: All three Corvale sites receive atenolol 25 mg tablets labeled by Bryant Ranch Prepack (NDC 71335153501).
rejected.reason: "three" is a number in words; numbers must be digits from the evidence

rejected.text: An earlier inspection in 2009 resulted in an OAI classification and a Warning Letter in 2010, but the most recent inspection is VAI.
rejected.reason: causal claim ("resulted in") that the cited record does not make
